previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy status was admitted after transfer for a clogged GJ tube. He had recently been treated for aspiration pneumonia with Unasyn and was weaned from mechanical ventilation and pressors prior to admission. The clogged feeding tube was successfully replaced via interventional radiology, allowing resumption of tube feeds and oral medications, including antiretroviral therapy. Mild transaminitis was noted with ultrasound showing gallstones but no cholecystitis; outpatient follow-up was recommended. He remained stable on trach collar with no respiratory deterioration. He was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing monitoring of liver enzymes and continuation of chronic medications.
problems: Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase and lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
Calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis without obstruction

EXAMINATION:  Chest x-ray

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with L PICC// CONFIRM PLACEMENT   Contact name:

COMPARISON:  Previous x-ray from ___

FINDINGS: 

There is a left PICC with the tip in the region of the cavoatrial junction. 
There is a tracheostomy tube, similar in position to prior.  Low lung volumes
compromise evaluation.  There is persistent diffuse bilateral interstitial
opacities.  Allowing for differences in technique, this not significantly
changed.  There are no large pleural effusions.  Heart size appear similar.

IMPRESSION: 

Left PICC tip in region of kv O2 junction.  Heart and lungs appear similar to
the prior study from ___.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with malfunctioning GJ tube at OSH. Has foley in
place.// Please replace GJ tube

COMPARISON:  GJ tube exchange ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology
Fellow and Dr. ___, attending radiologist performed the
procedure. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the key
components of the procedure and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's
findings.
ANESTHESIA: 1% lidocaine was used for local anesthesia
MEDICATIONS: None.
CONTRAST:  20 ml of Optiray
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  4.9 min, 27 mGy

PROCEDURE:  18 ___, 3.5 cm stoma length low profile gastrojejunostomy tube
exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
health care proxy. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and
placed supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per
___ protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.

The existing Foley tube was injected with contrast and showed opacification of
the gastric rugae and duodenum.  A stiff glidewire was negotiated into the
stomach.  The balloon of the Foley was taken down and the catheter was removed
over the wire.  A 5 ___ Kumpe the catheter was advanced over the wire into
the stomach and negotiated into the jejunum with the Glidewire.  Position was
confirmed with contrast injection.  The Kumpe the was removed over the
Glidewire.  A new, 18 ___, 3.5 cm stoma length low profile
gastrojejunostomy tube was advanced over the wire into position under
fluoroscopy.  The balloon was inflated under fluoroscopic visualization. 
Contrast was administered through the jejunostomy and gastrostomy lumens to
confirm appropriate positioning.  The lumens were flushed and capped.  The
site was dressed.  The patient tolerated the procedure well without any
immediate complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Appropriately positioned new 18 ___ low profile gastrojejunostomy tube.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful exchange of a gastrojejunostomy tube for a new 18 ___, 3.5 cm
stoma length low-profile MIC gastrojejunostomy tube. The tube is ready to use.
